controller_actions.task: Rewrite module.py so it exposes solve(data) per the user contract: data is {"width": int, "requests": list of int}. Raise ValueError if width < 1. Bucket each timestamp t as t // width (floor division, correct for negative t). Count requests per bucket, and return one entry per non-empty bucket as {"bucket": index, "start": index * width, "count": n}, sorted by bucket ascending. Repeated timestamps each count. Empty requests returns []. Do not mutate the input. Use only Python standard library imports from the allowed list, with no I/O or dynamic code execution. Only edit module.py. The current version is wrong: it returns one entry per request instead of aggregating by bucket and does not validate width.

Write test_cases.json for solve(data) per the user contract: data is {"width": int, "requests": list of int}. Output a JSON list of at least four distinct cases. Each case has "input" plus exactly one of "output" (expected JSON result) or "error" (exception class name). Include: an empty request list returning []; repeated identical timestamps counting each; negative timestamps bucketed with floor division (e.g. width 5, requests [-1, -5, -6] gives buckets -1, -1, -2 with starts -5, -5, -10); a width below 1 raising ValueError (e.g. width 0 gives error "ValueError"); and a multi-bucket case with unsorted requests returning buckets sorted ascending. Make sure every expected output matches the contract exactly, with start = bucket * width. Only edit test_cases.json.
